note: It's Thanksgiving weekend in the US, so feeds were thinner and heavier on Black Friday deals, which are filtered out here.

front.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn't a virtue
front.tldr: Anthropic went public the same day Grand Theft Auto VI became one of the most successful entertainment launches ever, a reminder that painstaking, inefficient human craft still beats pure optimisation.

front.title: SpaceX gets FCC approval to deploy 1 million satellites for its AI orbital data center
front.tldr: The FCC has approved SpaceX's plan to put 1 million satellites into orbit to build an AI data centre in space, a vast bet on computing beyond Earth.

front.title: MacRemote: Connect Any Agent to Your Mac's Tools, Now Free and Open Source
front.tldr: A MacStories developer has released MacRemote, a free, open source Mac app that lets any AI agent securely use a Mac's tools and local MCPs, six months in the making.

stories.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
stories.tldr: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the US tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.

stories.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
stories.tldr: Simon Willison flags sqlite3_rsync, SQLite's remote copy tool, added as experimental in 2024 and since improved, for syncing databases efficiently between machines.

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.tldr: Simon Willison notes the New York Times is telling contracted photographers not to update Photoshop, after its new AI features raised concerns flagged on Hacker News.

stories.title: Quoting Jack Despain Zhou
stories.tldr: Simon Willison quotes Jack Despain Zhou on AI's de-individualising effect: hearing the same Claude-shaped voice in YouTube videos, conference talks and emails alike.

stories.title: A month with the iPhone Duo has changed how I use my phone
stories.tldr: A TechCrunch writer says a month with Apple's folding iPhone Duo pushed them to read more books and break mindless scrolling habits.

stories.title: The Screens app will let you turn your iPhone Duo into an itty bitty MacBook
stories.tldr: Edovia has added a Laptop Mode to its Screens remote desktop app, letting iPhone Duo owners control a Mac from the folding phone's two screens.

stories.title: X finally gets parental controls after 20 years
stories.tldr: X has added parental controls for teenagers after two decades without them, giving parents tools to manage what their children see on the platform.

stories.title: Readdle's Documents app adds voice recording with transcripts, summaries, more
stories.tldr: Readdle has updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad with Voice Notes, letting users record conversations and automatically generate transcripts and summaries.

stories.title: Halide Adds Fill Light Feature for iPhone Duo
stories.tldr: Halide 3.4 can use the iPhone Duo's outer display as a fill light when the phone is unfolded, offering softer lighting than the built-in flash.

stories.title: Obvious Affordances Are Due for a Comeback
stories.tldr: A Daring Fireball post argues interface design is overdue a return to obvious, clickable-looking affordances, after years of flat design hiding what can actually be tapped.

stories.title: 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Devouring $85M Over Thanksgiving Weekend
stories.tldr: Lionsgate's prequel is on track for an $85m Thanksgiving weekend, aiming to beat its own series record after a strong Monday and Tuesday debut.

stories.title: Chiwetel Ejiofor on How Stephen Frears' 'Dirty Pretty Things' Led Him to Fall in Love With Film
stories.tldr: Chiwetel Ejiofor traces his love of film to working with Stephen Frears on Dirty Pretty Things, after his screen debut alongside Steven Spielberg on Amistad.

stories.title: Robert Aramayo's Star-Making Turn in 'I Swear' Is Already Award-Winning, Now He Just Wants People to See It
stories.tldr: Robert Aramayo won two BAFTAs for I Swear and tells IndieWire the next step is simply getting more people to watch it, not more acclaim.

stories.title: Michel Hazanavicius To Present Exclusive Footage Of 'The Third Hand' In AI Case Study At Les Arcs
stories.tldr: Oscar-winning director Michel Hazanavicius will show unseen footage from his upcoming film The Third Hand as part of an AI case study at December's Les Arcs festival.

stories.title: 'The Lowdown' Season 2 Finale Hinges on Two Monologues: Ethan Hawke and Sterlin Harjo Break Them Down
stories.tldr: Creator Sterlin Harjo and star Ethan Hawke explain how they built the finale's two pivotal monologues, one written as a homage to No Country for Old Men.

stories.title: Bill Simmons: Last year's Jaylen Brown played better than this year's Jayson Tatum
stories.tldr: Bill Simmons says last year's Jaylen Brown was playing better than this year's Jayson Tatum, criticising the shots Tatum is taking in Boston's offence.

stories.title: 3 to Watch: Patriots Look to Get Back on Track in Los Angeles vs. Chargers
stories.tldr: The 5-5 Patriots travel to face the 1-9 Chargers looking to end a two-game losing streak, with three storylines to watch in the Week 12 matchup.

stories.title: How does Aaron Rodgers' shocking release impact the Patriots?
stories.tldr: Aaron Rodgers' release from the Steelers could help New England's playoff hopes, since the Patriots trail Pittsburgh in the race for a wildcard spot.

stories.title: What Romeo Doubs returning to practice means for the Patriots
stories.tldr: Wide receiver Romeo Doubs returned to Patriots practice this week, one of two starters back from injured reserve while the offence still waits on quarterback Drake Maye.

stories.title: Haas finally confirms Bearman's new contract for 2027
stories.tldr: Haas has confirmed Oliver Bearman will stay for 2027 alongside Rafael Camara, completing the Formula 1 grid for next season with two Ferrari junior drivers.

stories.title: Max Verstappen details his ideal 2030 F1 Formula
stories.tldr: Fresh off winning a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen laid out his vision for Formula 1's 2030 rules: lighter cars, simpler engines and a push-to-pass system.

stories.title: Alonso to not let his age determine F1 retirement
stories.tldr: Fernando Alonso, F1's most experienced driver, says he will retire once he feels slow, not because of his age, and doesn't need a footballer's fitness to compete.

read.why: A nice reminder to pause and celebrate milestones before getting back to work, fitting for Thanksgiving weekend and Damian's own side projects.
read.subtitle: Taking a moment to celebrate and reflect—and then back to work

listen.why: Garfield's rise from poverty rewards patient, unglamorous effort, the same theme running through today's lead story on craft beating efficiency.
listen.title: #438 James Garfield's Extraordinary Rise

listen.why: Travis Kalanick on building Atoms after Uber, a founder still obsessed with hard, unglamorous problems, fitting today's theme of effort over efficiency.
listen.title: Travis Kalanick, Founder of Uber & Atoms

listen.why: Steve Ballmer on building and leading Microsoft, fitting Damian's interest in the great product operators alongside Jobs and Disney.
listen.title: The Steve Ballmer Interview

finally.title: Victorian hospital conversion in Edinburgh named Scotland's best new building
finally.tldr: An old Victorian infirmary turned into an educational space by Bennetts Associates has won the Andrew Doolan award for Scotland's best new building of 2026.
